summary.intent: Diagnose and fix failing desktop e2e cross-client sync tests on macOS and Linux that were introduced by a recently merged PR (#454).
summary.outcome: Fixed the immediate test failure by adding `ls` to the polling loop, added Windows parity (new test-cross-client-sync.ps1 + run-all.ps1 step), and improved the FUSE layer so file access (lookup/open) also triggers metadata staleness checks — not just readdir. All changes committed and pushed as a PR.

repo: FUSE metadata refresh is triggered exclusively by readdir (drain_refresh_completions → populate_folder), not by getattr or lookup on already-loaded folders.
DIR_TTL is 0s so directory reads always reach FUSE; FILE_TTL is 60s so stat/cat may be served from kernel cache for up to 60 seconds.
Windows test suite (run-all.ps1) was missing the cross-client sync test entirely — Step 6 did not exist, which is why CI showed Windows 'passing'.
Project uses a monorepo with packages under packages/ and crates/ (Rust FUSE layer at crates/fuse/src/), and desktop e2e scripts under tests/desktop-e2e/scripts/.
Refresh is two-phase and non-blocking: first access after TTL expiry spawns the fetch, the next access applies it.

code.finding: handle_lookup only triggered background fetch for unloaded folders (lazy load), never for stale already-loaded folders. Fix adds a staleness check mirroring readdir's populate_folder pattern.
handle_open on Windows had no drain_refresh_completions call and no staleness check for the parent folder. Fix adds both, matching the macOS/Linux handle_lookup improvement.
Test 5 polling loop used only stat + cat, never ls. Added ls "$MP" before stat/cat to trigger readdir and allow FUSE to detect modified_at changes.
readdir handler calls drain_refresh_completions() then populate_folder(), which compares modified_at timestamps and marks files for re-resolution — the only pre-fix path that detected remote edits.

workflow: When a cross-platform test suite has platform-specific scripts, always verify all platforms have equivalent coverage — a missing PS1 file silently made Windows appear to pass.
Checking kernel-level TTL constants (FILE_TTL vs DIR_TTL) is essential when debugging FUSE polling issues; stat/cat may never reach FUSE if kernel cache is warm.
cargo build --features fuse and cargo test --features fuse are the correct commands for validating the FUSE crate on macOS/Linux; WinFsp feature cannot be verified on macOS.

friction: Local main branch had diverged from origin/main (1 vs 6 commits), causing git pull to fail twice until the divergence was resolved.
Files from the merged PR were not present locally, requiring all reads to be done via git show origin/main:<path> rather than direct file reads.
WinFsp (Windows) FUSE feature could not be compiled or tested on macOS, so the Windows read_ops.rs change could only be visually reviewed.
open_items: The FUSE refresh is still two-phase (spawn on first stale access, apply on next access) — a true background polling thread would give fully automatic sync without requiring any user file access.
File managers like Finder/Nautilus trigger continuous readdir on visible directories, but CLI/editor workflows still rely on the 60s kernel TTL expiry before the new lookup staleness check kicks in.
Windows test-cross-client-sync.ps1 was created but could not be end-to-end validated in CI before the PR was submitted.
